notes: Four-condition transition study of SPEC section 39, run here on labeled synthetic data as a pipeline demonstration. Conditions share the same start probe and designed target; only the induced route differs. v2.1: predicted_intermediate corrected to a true shortest-route waypoint (Fi for the IEE reference TIM); the former Fe condition is retained as chord_assisted, an explicitly Model G (M4) prediction distinct from the M3 routing-distance hypothesis.

predicted_intermediate.rationale: for the IEE reference TIM, Fi lies on a shortest Ne-Ti route of the pure routing cube (routing distance Ne-Ti = 2; the shortest-route intermediates are exactly Fi and Se); waypoint completion length equals the direct distance

chord_assisted.rationale: Fe is NOT on a shortest Ne-Ti route of the pure routing cube (waypoint completion length 4); it is reachable in one step only via the directed Model G chord Ne->Fe, after which Fe-Ti is a primitive edge (hybrid length 2). This condition tests the M4 hybrid-graph prediction, not the M3 routing-distance prediction.

control_intermediate.rationale: matched-length control: Ni is on no shortest Ne-Ti route in either the pure routing cube or the hybrid graph for the reference TIM (waypoint completion length 4 in both)

predicted_ordering: direct <= predicted_intermediate < control_intermediate on log latency (H2, pure routing cube)
chord_assisted < control_intermediate iff the hybrid-graph (M4) mechanism is real; chord_assisted ~ control_intermediate under pure M3 routing
